purpose: Add eight source-exact Philip P. Bliss biographical and hymn-ministry excerpts for family worship, sacred song, consecration, calling, evangelism, and Christian service.

defaults.author: D. W. Whittle
defaults.rightsBasis: This 1877 A. S. Barnes memorial edition is public domain in the United States; every excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the page scan before publication.

entries.title: Always Trusting, Always Singing
entries.text: He lived in continual communion with his Savior; always happy, always trusting, always singing.
entries.slideText: always happy, always trusting, always singing
entries.author: Philip P. Bliss, quoted by D. W. Whittle
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed remembrance of Bliss's father in a message on abiding fellowship, trust, or a singing Christian home.
entries.reviewNote: This is a son's remembrance, not a claim of sinless constancy. Define communion and joy from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: His First Memory of His Father
entries.text: My first recollection of him is his daily family prayer.
entries.slideText: My first recollection of him is his daily family prayer.
entries.author: Philip P. Bliss, quoted by D. W. Whittle
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed biographical illustration of the lasting memory created by ordinary family prayer.
entries.reviewNote: The daily pattern is descriptive testimony. Teach parental responsibility and household devotion from KJV Scripture.

entries.title: Character That Shaped a Son
entries.text: His character and example had much to do in moulding the character of his son.
entries.slideText: His character and example had much to do in moulding the character of his son.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed biographical observation about the influence of a godly example across generations.
entries.reviewNote: Do not promise identical outcomes for every child. Ground the call to godly example in the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: The Power of Song to Impress the Gospel
entries.text: what a power has song to impress the Gospel.
entries.slideText: what a power has song to impress the Gospel
entries.author: Darwin Cook, quoted by D. W. Whittle
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed historical reflection on sacred song reinforcing gospel truth in the hearer's memory.
entries.reviewNote: Song may impress truth but cannot replace the preached word or the Spirit's work. Test lyrics by KJV Scripture.

entries.title: Consecrated and Worshipful Music
entries.text: all music in connection with worship, whether by instrument or voice, should be consecrated and worshipful.
entries.author: E. P. Goodwin
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed historic pastoral standard for discussing the purpose and character of church music.
entries.reviewNote: Apply the principle through clear biblical teaching, not taste alone. Evaluate worship by the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: The Aim of Sacred Selections
entries.text: selections aimed at honoring God, exalting Jesus Christ, magnifying His Gospel
entries.slideText: honoring God, exalting Jesus Christ, magnifying His Gospel
entries.author: E. P. Goodwin
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed three-part test of the stated purpose behind congregational and special music.
entries.reviewNote: This concise historical standard is subordinate to Scripture. Examine both the words and ministry practice by KJV truth.

entries.title: The Joy of Being Christ's Servant
entries.text: nothing compared with the joy of being a servant of Jesus Christ, and the gladness of being used to impart life by the Gospel to dead souls.
entries.slideText: the joy of being a servant of Jesus Christ
entries.recommendedUse: Use as Whittle's attributed assessment of Bliss's surrender of income and professional ambition for evangelistic service.
entries.reviewNote: Only God gives spiritual life; the excerpt describes gospel instrumentality. Do not imply that vocational ministry is a higher class of discipleship.

entries.title: Gifts Shining Through a Christian Life
entries.text: how beautiful the gifts of God may become when shining out through a Christian life
entries.slideText: how beautiful the gifts of God may become when shining out through a Christian life
entries.sourceLocator: Mr. Bliss as an Evangelist, page 56
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed concluding observation on talent yielded to God through Christian character and service.
entries.reviewNote: Do not confuse natural talent with spiritual maturity. Teach gifts, stewardship, and God's glory from the cited KJV passages.
